The functions f and g are defined by
$\mathrm{f}(x) = 9 - x^2 \qquad x \in \mathbb{R} \quad x \geqslant 0$
$\mathrm{g}(x) = \frac{3}{2x+1} \qquad x \in \mathbb{R} \quad x \geqslant 0$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down the range of f
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: B1: Correct range. Allow equivalent notation e.g. $y \leqslant 9$, $\mathrm{f} \leqslant 9$, $y \in (-\infty, 9]$ but not $x \leqslant 9$. Condone just "$\leqslant 9$" and "less than or equal to 9"

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the value of $\mathrm{fg}(1.5)$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Full attempt at method to find fg(1.5) condoning slips. Implied by a correct answer or 8.44 e.g. For a correct order of operations so requires an attempt to apply g(1.5) first and then f to their g(1.5). Also allow for an attempt to substitute $x=1.5$ into $9-\left(\frac{3}{2x+1}\right)^2$ condoning slips such as substituting $x=1.5$ into $9-\frac{3}{(2x+1)^2}$
A1: $\frac{135}{16}$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\mathrm{fg}(1.5)=\mathrm{f}\left(\frac{3}{2\times1.5+1}\right)=9-\left(\frac{3}{2\times1.5+1}\right)^2$ M1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find $\mathrm{g}^{-1}$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Changes the subject of $y=\frac{3}{2x+1}$ and obtains $x=\frac{3\pm y}{2y}$ or $x=\frac{3}{2y}\pm\frac{1}{2}$ or equivalent. Alternatively changes the subject of $x=\frac{3}{2y+1}$ and obtains $y=\frac{3\pm x}{2x}$ or $y=\frac{3}{2x}\pm\frac{1}{2}$ or equivalent.
A1: $\mathrm{g}^{-1}(x)=\frac{3-x}{2x}$, $\mathrm{g}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{3-x}{x}\right)$, $\mathrm{g}^{-1}(x)=\frac{3}{2x}-\frac{1}{2}$, $\mathrm{g}^{-1}: x \mapsto \frac{3-x}{2x}$ or $\mathrm{g}^{-1}: x \mapsto \frac{3}{2x}-\frac{1}{2}$. Condone $y=\frac{3-x}{2x}$ o.e. and even $\mathrm{g}^{-1}=\frac{3-x}{2x}$ but NOT $\mathrm{f}^{-1}=\frac{3-x}{2x}$ o.e. ISW after a correct answer. B1: Correct domain. Allow equivalent notation e.g. $x \in (0,3]$ but not just $(0,3]$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\mathrm{g}(x)=\frac{3}{2x+1}\Rightarrow \mathrm{g}^{-1}(x)=\frac{3-x}{2x}$ M1 A1; $0<x\leqslant 3$ B1

(2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence, or otherwise, express $y$ in the form $kb^x$, giving the values of the constants $k$ and $b$ to 3 significant figures.
(3)

M1: "Removes" the logs in their equation. e.g. $\log_{10} y = \text{"}m\text{"}x+\text{"}c\text{"} \Rightarrow y=10^{\text{"}m\text{"}x+\text{"}c\text{"}}$
M1: "Correct" strategy to obtain values of $k$ and $b$ or else proceeding correctly to a form $y=10^{\text{"}\frac{5}{16}\text{"}x}\times 10^{\text{"}1.5\text{"}}$. A1: Correct equation produced, $y=31.6\times 2.05^x$, and no errors seen. This will score Special case: M0 M1 A0.
Alternative Method: Starting with $y=kb^x$
M1: Takes logs of both sides and applies at least one correct log law e.g. $\log_{(10)} kb^x=\log_{(10)}k+\log_{(10)}b^x$, $\log_{(10)}b^x=x\log_{(10)}b$

M1: Complete method for finding A, B, C and D. For example substitution/comparing coefficients/long division. parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Prove that
$\cot^2 x - \tan^2 x \equiv 4\cot 2x \csc 2x \qquad x \neq \frac{n\pi}{2} \quad n \in \mathbb{Z}$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Way One (LHS to RHS)
M1: Changes the LHS to $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ and attempts to make a single fraction using a correct common denominator. Condone errors/slips on the numerator: $\cot^2 x-\tan^2 x \equiv \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x}-\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} \equiv \frac{\cos^4 x-\sin^4 x}{\sin^2 x\cos^2 x}$
dM1: Attempts/applies either $\cos^4 x-\sin^4 x=(\cos^2 x-\sin^2 x)(\cos^2 x+\sin^2 x)=\cos^2 x-\sin^2 x=\cos 2x$ on the numerator, or $\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x$ to the denominator condoning bracketing slip: $\equiv \frac{(\cos^2 x-\sin^2 x)(\cos^2 x+\sin^2 x)}{\sin^2 x\cos^2 x} \equiv \frac{\cos 2x}{...}$ or $\frac{...}{\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin 2x\right)^2}$
A1: Applies both of the above correctly to achieve a correct expression in terms of $\cos 2x$ and $\sin 2x$: $\equiv \frac{\cos 2x}{\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin 2x\right)^2}$
A1*: Reaches the right hand side with sufficient working shown: $\equiv 4\frac{\cos 2x}{\sin 2x \sin 2x} \equiv 4\cot 2x \csc 2x$. Expect to see $\sin^2 2x$ split into $\sin 2x \sin 2x$. Penalise consistent (not once or twice) use of poor notation on this mark only.
